title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
technique: unified block-sparse attention: static streaming heads (half of heads) + dynamic hierarchical KV page selection with reuse, plus KV quantization, in fused kernels for prefill and decode

optimized_metrics.evidence: For the prefilling stage, we use time-to-first-token (TTFT) as a key metric
for the decoding stage, we emphasize minimizing the per-token generation latency.
Our primary focus is on serving throughput.
without sacrificing the long-context capabilities of the original dense, floating-point models

headline_claim.text: On average, LServe accelerates LLM prefilling by up to 2.9x and decoding by 1.3-2.1x over vLLM, maintaining long-context accuracy.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 10 (relative decoding throughput normalized to LServe), Fig 11 (prefill speed)
Tables 2-4, Fig 9 (LongBench, RULER, NIAH, AIME, MATH500)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For the prefilling stage, we use time-to-first-token (TTFT) as a key metric
metric_definitions.notes: Not formally defined; Fig 11 plots prefilling speed normalized to LServe. Offline single-request long-context prefill; no queueing.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: for the decoding stage, we emphasize minimizing the per-token generation latency
metric_definitions.notes: Fig 10 y-axis is 'relative throughput of each system, normalized by the speed of LServe'; per-step decode latency in ms/step used in §3.5 with batch size 32.

load_regime: fixed batch size / batch=1 style kernel benchmarks at fixed context lengths (16K-512K); no request-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Small accuracy deltas vs dense (LongBench avg 38.9 -> 38.6 on Llama-3-8B); larger token budget (8192 vs 4096) up to 6% slower
workloads: LongBench, RULER, NIAH, AIME2024, MATH500; synthetic fixed-length sequences for speed
extractor_notes: Kernel/system speed paper, not request-level serving. No percentiles, SLOs, or arrival process. Two-column text extraction; metrics paragraph says 'Our primary focus is on serving throughput' but plots are speed ratios, not tokens/s values.
load_class_quote: Figure 10: Decoding Speed Evaluation. The y-axis indicates the relative throughput of each system, normalized by the speed of LServe. (§4.3; fixed context lengths, no request-rate sweep; ablations at unit batch size)
